The total length of the animal ranged from 35 to 40 centimeters, with males reaching about 1.3 kilograms and females about 1 kilogram.

Hunters exploited the bird's attraction to red objects by using colored cloth to lure them before striking with sticks.
While commonly placed in its own genus Aphanapteryx, it has historically been grouped with the Rodrigues rail in the genus Erythromachus.
